additional_info.subject: Cust receiving low power than expected - Siemens Sicharge D at R&R Tapah, Malaysia
additional_info.body:
Dear Siemens support,
My name is Hafizi from TNBX, the Charge Point Operator for TNB Electron.
I would like to lodge a complaint received from a customer that charged at R&R Tapah Northbound, Malaysia that equipped with your 180kW Siemens Sicharge D charger. Please find below the details of the issue.
Charging session
: March 13, 2025 2:07 PM - 2:34 PM
Location
: R&R Tapah Northbound (TNB Electron)
Connector
: 2 (being limited to 100kW)
Car
: Tesla Model Y
Start SoC
: 26%
End SoC
: 66%
Complaint
: The overall session of the customer is only receiving 47kW and less, and not the expected 100kW. The EV also charging in low SoC, hence should be receiving more power.
Notes
: During the Tesla Model Y session, there is also an ongoing session on Connector 1.
Therefore, we would like your team to investigate why the customer received low power, and can’t reach near 100kW .
Looking forward for your findings.
Thank you.
Regards,
MUHD AMIRUL HAFIZI BIN SUKOR

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0413331-DC/Si-D/MY-{Null] customer received low power CRM:02682000005
additional_info.body:
Hello Edna,
Hope you are doing well.
We have checked the detailed logs of charging session started at
06:07:27
UTC time on 13th Mar.
Initially EV provided his Maximum Voltage as 430 V and Maximum Current as 499 A, which calculates to 214 kW maximum Power.
But during charging EV never demanded more than 165 A, which is denoted by EVTragetCurrent. [DC2]
During charging-
2025-03 13T06:07:13|
DC2
|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=100|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=163|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=41.5|EVSE_NowCur[A]=113|EVSE_NowVol[V]=366|EV_TarCur[A]=127|EV_TarVol[V]=430|EV_SOC[%]=41|
EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=59
|Pilot=4
When charging session stopped-
DESpwr[kW]=75
2025-03-13T06:33:50.853538+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] |2025-03-13T06:07:13|
DC2
|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=100|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=207|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=55.9|EVSE_NowCur[A]=151|EVSE_NowVol[V]=370|
EV_TarCur[A]=165
|EV_TarVol[V]=430|EV_SOC[%]=66|EVSE_D
ESpwr[kW]=75|
Pilot=4
In this charging session Target current set by EV was low that's why the output power was less than expected.
Furthermore, we checked the recent charging session logs, and the charger always provides a current equal to the EVTargetCurrent.
2025-03-24T05:50:53|DC2|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=100|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=244|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=99.1|EVSE_NowCur[A]=242|EVSE_NowVol[V]=409|EV_TarCur[A]=244|EV_TarVol[V]=478|EV_SOC[%]=30|
EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=100|
Pilot=4
2025-03-22T14:27:34|DC2|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=100|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=130|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=41.4|EVSE_NowCur[A]=94|EVSE_NowVol[V]=438|EV_TarCur[A]=95|EV_TarVol[V]=456|EV_SOC[%]=76|
EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=100|
Pilot=4
Keys-
EV_TarCur[A]=is current demanded by EV.
EV_TarVol[V]=is Voltage at which EV will be 100% charged.
EV_SOC[%]= is current State of Charge of EV
EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=Charger's Dynamic Energy Sharing power.
Hope this answers your query, if you have any other questions, please let us know. If not, can we close this ticket?
Regards,
Beerpal Singh
eMobility Support
